Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Rootopia (development version)

  • New network_metrics(). Summarizes any segment network given as an edge table: nodes, edges, components, tips, branch points, and the alpha, beta and gamma connectivity coefficients. The topology argument decides whether loop metrics are reported as traits ("reticulate", e.g. mycelium or leaf venation) or under $qc ("tree", where they are identities, and "projected_tree", where a loop is two roots crossing in projection and the count becomes a segmentation diagnostic).

  • New root_transport(). For every segment in an edge table it reports the path length and Hagen-Poiseuille path resistance from the base of its root system, and the number of tips, the root length and the lateral surface area that lie beyond it. Each component is rooted at its thickest free end, the same convention the Strahler ordering uses. Segments on a cycle have no subtree and get NA with a warning.

  • render_order_overlay() paints continuous per-segment values, not only branch orders. It picks the legend from the data – one labelled swatch per order for small integers, a viridis ramp with a scale bar otherwise – and continuous, value_label and n_bins control it. The first argument is renamed from tip_order to values; the old name still works and warns.

  • convert_root_units() and branch_order_map() default to length_method = "kimura". The previous default, the sqrt(2) chain code, walks the skeleton pixel to pixel and so traces a staircase rather than the line it represents. Measured against digital straight lines of known length it runs about 5.7% long on average, up to 8.2% near 22.5 degrees, and zero only for exactly horizontal or vertical segments; Kimura’s estimator reduces that to about 1.8%. This changes reported root length, and everything derived from it, by a few percent. Pass length_method = "polyline" to reproduce earlier output.

  • image_threshold(method = "adaptive") gains adaptive_k, the multiple of the local mean a pixel must reach, defaulting to 1.15. The adaptive rule compares a pixel against the mean of its own neighborhood, and a window holding only background averages to the background level, so a multiplier at or below 1 marks half or more of a root-free area as root. Measured on synthetic scans with a 5% background coefficient of variation, a multiplier of 1.15 leaves 0.1% of a root-free patch marked where 1.05 leaves 16% and 0.4 leaves all of it. Across root/background contrasts of 1.3 to 2.2 and background CVs of 2% to 10% the best value fell between 1.05 and 1.30. Values at or below 1 warn, and threshold – a fraction of the global maximum, used by the global and deblur modes – warns rather than being silently ignored when passed alongside method = "adaptive".

  • image_threshold() raises the window_size default from 15 to 51. The local mean includes the pixel under test together with its root, so a root filling much of its own window raises the level it is judged against and is rejected. On synthetic scans with roots up to 9 px wide, the best F1 against a known mask was 0.54 at a window of 15, 0.90 at 51 and 0.96 at 101. A window wider than the image is clamped to the largest odd window that fits, with a warning, instead of reaching terra::focal() and failing there.

  • ?image_threshold states what neither method can do. Both mark pixels brighter than a reference, so where root and soil are equally bright the useful range for adaptive_k is empty and no setting works. Measured against its own segmentation, the bundled minirhizotron scan has roots averaging 1.07 times the soil brightness while the soil’s coefficient of variation runs from 0.23 to 0.93 across the frame; adaptive thresholding reaches an F1 of about 0.1 there. The adaptive example runs on a small synthetic gradient instead, where both conditions hold and the three roots are recovered exactly.

  • image_threshold(method = "adaptive") computes the local mean as two 1-D terra::focal() passes rather than one square kernel. A box mean is separable, so the work per pixel is proportional to the window side instead of its square: on a 1000 x 1000 raster the local mean takes 0.73 s at a window of 101 where a square kernel takes 29 s. Results are identical to machine precision when no cell is NA.

  • clean_image() renames max_hole_size to fill_holes_upto and max_artifact_size to drop_objects_upto. The old names said how big a thing was but not what happened to it; the new ones state that anything larger is left alone. The old names still work and warn.

  • clean_image() gains size_unit and dpi. With size_unit = "mm2" the thresholds are physical areas rather than pixel counts, so the same call cleans the same physical size whether a scan is 300 or 1200 dpi.

  • root_depth_metrics() / batch_root_traits() rename clean_max_hole_size to clean_fill_holes_upto and clean_max_artifact_size to clean_drop_objects_upto, and gain clean_size_unit. The old names still work and warn.

  • root_depth_metrics() validates the cleaning thresholds before the image loop. A non-numeric or NA threshold now stops with a message naming the argument, where it previously failed inside the per-image tryCatch and left the image silently uncleaned. NULL means no limit and switches cleaning on, matching clean_image().

Rootopia 1.1.0

Beta release, available from the GitHub repository only. Not submitted to CRAN.

  • Requires R >= 4.1 (the package uses the native |> pipe) and terra >= 1.8.
